Verifies that the covariance between a constant series and any other series is zero, because a constant has no variance.

Verifies that a dataset with only one column produces a 1×1 covariance matrix whose sole entry equals the (population) variance of that column.

With {@code biasCorrected=false}, two observations [1, 2] have variance ((1-1.5)²+(2-1.5)²)/2 = 0.25.
Two observations, one variable, no bias correction

Verifies that passing arrays too small for the requested computation throws the appropriate exceptions:
  • A single-element array pair requires at least 2 observations for bias-uncorrected covariance → {@link MathIllegalArgumentException}.
  • An empty column array → {@link NotStrictlyPositiveException}.
Expected: need at least 2 observations
Expected: column length must be > 0

Verifies internal consistency of {@link Covariance}:
  1. Diagonal entries of the covariance matrix equal the column variances.
  2. The matrix is symmetric (C[i,j] == C[j,i]).
  3. Off-diagonal entries match pairwise {@code covariance(col_i, col_j)}.
  4. When all columns are identical, every matrix entry equals the column variance.
  5. Bias-correction defaults: {@code computeCovarianceMatrix(data)} and {@code computeCovarianceMatrix(data, true)} produce the same result.
  6. One-arg {@code covariance(x, y)} equals {@code covariance(x, y, true)}.
1. Diagonal entries must equal column variances
2 & 3. Symmetry and agreement with pairwise covariance computation
4. All-identical columns: every entry in the covariance matrix equals the shared column variance
5. Bias-correction default: computeCovarianceMatrix(data) == computeCovarianceMatrix(data, true)
6. One-arg covariance(x, y) defaults to bias-corrected (biasCorrected=true)
